title: Nvidia Launches Nemotron 3.5 Super VL Open 120B Agent Model
summary:
This multimodal system combines reasoning and tool use to power autonomous AI agents capable of interpreting images, video, and documents natively. The model uses a Mixture-of-Experts architecture with 120B total parameters and 12B active per token, featuring a 1M token context window for long-running workflows. Nvidia released the weights, data, and recipes openly via Hugging Face, with day 0 deployment on platforms including Baseten, fal, OpenRouter, and Together AI. The system completes 10,000 coding tasks up to 4x faster and scores 51.78% on SWE-bench Pro.

The update also includes the Nemotron 3.5 Bolt and Lightning models, the latter being a 30B parameter text-only system. The Super VL model is highly optimized for Blackwell GPUs using NVFP4 quantization, which Lambda reports can reach a peak output of 1,860 tok/s on a single GPU. Nvidia trained the architecture across GB200 and GB300 hardware to eliminate the need to pass context between separate text and vision models.

selectedTweets.text:
Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is the latest open model from @NVIDIA with vision built in natively (120B total, 12B active per token, 1M-token context, text + image + document + GUI + video input).

We benchmarked both deployment paths on Lambda with @sglang_proj:

* NVFP4 on 1× NVIDIA Blackwell GPU, 1,860 tok/s peak (C16), 587 tok/s/user (C1)

* BF16 on 2× NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs, 1,669 tok/s peak (C16), 530 tok/s/user (C1)

One NVIDIA Blackwell GPU at NVFP4 out-throughputs two NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs at BF16 on the same 8,192-in / 1,024-out workload, roughly 2.2× the per-GPU throughput, because Blackwell runs FP4 natively.

Both deployments run speculative decoding with multi-token prediction (EAGLE, 5 steps, 6 draft tokens).

Model card and full deployment instructions at https://t.co/aMVK4yeFOP

selectedTweets.text:
Very excited to announce our new models: Nemotron 3.5 Super and Lightning! 

This also feels like a good time to share that a few months ago I joined the amazing Nemotron Pretraining team. We're cooking some very large and very strong models for you!

Here is a tech summary for 3.5:

* Super is a 120B total / 12B active vision language model (VLM)

* Lightning is a 30B total / 3B active text-only LLM

* Super scores 51.78% on SWE-bench Pro (better than Nemotron 3 Ultra despite ~4.6× fewer active params!)

* arch: MoE Hybrid Mamba-Transformer designed for efficient inference, with a 1M token ctx window, and native speculative decoding (via MTP)

* training is done across our GB200 and GB300 (and deployment validated across all imaginable SKUs, including consumer (RTX) and DGX Spark)

A few details on how we train these:

-- Pretraining

* pipeline: initialize with Nemotron 3 base -> custom MTP initialization + 100B-token MTP warm-up -> 1T-token distillation from the next larger N3 teacher

* Lightning then goes through a 21B token long-context (LC) stage (@ 1M ctx)

* Super goes through:

- Indic CPT: 100B tokens at 8K (10B Indic + 90B replay, we built a synthetic corpus with 2.83T toks across 22 Indian langs! Indic benchmarks improve by up to 9.82%)

- LC extension: 35B tokens at 1M

- Agentic SWE mid-training: 65.4B tokens at 256K (uses whole repos, issue-PR pairs, commit histories, etc.); DeepSWE pass@1 improves from 6.4 -> 10.4

- LC recovery: 9B tokens at 1M (as we observed regression after mid-training)

-- Post-training

* Super: two-stage SFT -> joint RLVR/RLHF -> specialist teachers -> two-stage MOPD -> MTP boosting

* Lightning uses a lighter text-only pipeline: single-stage SFT -> RLVR

* Super's SFT transforms the text-only base into a VLM using vision, agentic, reasoning, chat, safety, LC data

* A few examples of RLVR environments:

- Olympiad-level competitive programming

- Finance agents using SEC search, document parsing, evidence retrieval, and tool use

* Specialist teachers include Agentic, Reasoning, Video reasoning and tracking, Vision tool-use, Vision-reasoning, and an Alignment/RLHF teacher

* Two-stage MOPD consolidates these specialist capabilities into one model

* Post-training ends with MTP boosting to better align the drafter and reduce recursive train–inference mismatch; this improves Super's SPEED-Bench acceptance length by 21.8% (to 4.612 tokens)

-- Inference

The model is highly optimized for inference (with plenty of quantized options to choose from)! A few data points:

* On a GB200, Super reaches 4,856 output toks/s/GPU with ≥50 toks/s/user on a 20-turn agentic workload

* Super provides 2.34x the throughput of Qwen3.5 122B-A10B and 1.90x the throughput of Qwen3.8 Flash-Next

* Native MTP is complemented by standalone parallel drafters: LiLiCorr for Super, and DFlash and DSpark for Lightning

Looking forward to seeing what you do with 3.5! Phase shift for Nemotron incoming! :)) (with the usual this will be our weakest model ever, but really really so)
